sections.html:
Deeds for Lehigh County property are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds Division, Room 122 of the Lehigh County Courthouse, 455 W. Hamilton Street, Allentown, PA 18101. The phone number is 610-782-3162. Counter service runs Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30. Parcel identification, called GIS PIN certification, stops earlier, at 3:45 in the afternoon, so bring a deed that needs a new PIN in the morning or early afternoon.

The office closes on major holidays and on any day the President Judge of the Court of Common Pleas directs. Your closing agent normally files the deed and payoff papers for you. The fees below still matter, because each one appears as a line on your settlement statement.

A deed of any type costs $81.25 to record under the fee schedule effective January 1, 2026. That covers up to four pages, four names and one PIN certification. Anything beyond those limits is billed separately.

Lehigh County recording fees, effective January 1, 2026
DocumentFee
Deed, all types$81.25
Mortgage$81.25
Satisfaction piece$71.75
Release of mortgage$71.75
Assignment of mortgage$71.75
Deed of dedication$69.75
Easement or right-of-way$69.75
Quiet title action$28.50
Power of attorney$18.50

Extras are small but add up on a complicated parcel:

  • Each page over four costs $2.00, and each name over four costs $0.50.
  • Each additional PIN costs $10.00, so a deed that covers several parcels costs more.
  • Each electronic notation costs $2.00.
  • A rejected document costs $10.00 each time, and a returned check costs $20.00.
  • Mailing documents back costs $3.00 each unless you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

An overpayment of $10.00 or less is forfeited, and the office does not refund fees for a document sent twice by mistake. Check the amount before you send it.

Yes. The office accepts electronic filings through Simplifile, CSC and ePN. Those platforms calculate fees and taxes as you submit, so fewer documents get rejected, and electronic filings are usually recorded the same day. If one is rejected, you can correct it and send it back right away.

Maps and plans, including subdivision plats, can be recorded electronically through the same three vendors. The division keeps no paper copy of a map that was recorded electronically.

Certified copies cannot be bought online. They are made at the recorder's counter for $1.50 per document on top of the copy charge. Plain copies are $0.50 per page in person and $1.00 per page by mail.

The division holds records back to 1812. All of it is public except military discharge papers (DD-214), which the office records for free and keeps private. Staff are not authorized to do your search or research for you, so you search on your own. There are four ways to do it:

  • LANDEX Webstore: free searching, with a fee to view or print a document, aimed at occasional users.
  • LANDEX Remote: pay as you go at $0.15 a minute and $0.10 for each page loaded, built for heavy users, with an Index Book tab covering 1812 to 1983.
  • Lehigh County Online Records Access: needs an account and a yearly fee arranged through the county Fiscal Office.
  • In person: the public review area downstairs in the courthouse, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:00.

If you inherited a house with a thin paper trail, the index books can turn up an old deed or an unreleased mortgage before a buyer's title search does.

sections.h2: Transfer tax when a house sells
sections.html:
Pennsylvania charges 1 percent of the property's value on a transfer. You pay it at the recorder's counter on the day of filing, in the same payment as the recording fee. The state revenue department's page holds seller and buyer jointly responsible. Your school district and municipality may tack on a local share, and the rate depends on where the parcel sits. A city can charge differently than a township. Ask the recorder for the full combined rate on your parcel before you pick a list price.

Certain family transfers, transfers under a will or by intestacy, and transfers to government bodies are exempt. You explain a claimed exemption on the state's REV-183 Statement of Value.

sections.h2: Other filings that can land on a house record
sections.html:
A sale is not the only event that touches a parcel. Farmland owners record Act 319 preferential assessment filings at $33.00 with no extra charge for added pages or names, and covenant filings under Act 515 carry the same $33.00. An Agricultural Security Area ordinance costs $28.50. Easements and rights-of-way cost $69.75. A lease over 30 years costs $59.75. Financing statements under the Uniform Commercial Code cost $110.00 flat.

Release paperwork matters most to sellers. A paid-off mortgage keeps showing on the record until the lender files a satisfaction piece ($71.75) or release of mortgage ($71.75). If the house came to you by inheritance, search for loans that were paid years ago and never released. A notary commission and bond cost $33.50 in the same office.

Plans and maps follow a different scale. A subdivision, survey or stormwater plan costs $35.00 for page one and $25.00 for every page after it, and a condominium plan costs $40.00 and $25.00. Highway, mining and railroad maps cost $15.00 and $3.00. You would see them if you divide a lot before selling.

sections.h2: Steps from signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
A typical sale moves through the office in a few steps. Your title company or attorney drafts the deed and holds it to the four page, four name and one PIN limits. It is then sent through an e-recording vendor or walked to the Room 122 counter. The tax and the fee are collected in one payment. A deed that needs a new parcel number gets its GIS PIN certification first, which explains the earlier afternoon cutoff.

After acceptance the deed becomes part of the public record. Ask the closing agent for the recording details, and if a lender is being paid off, make sure its satisfaction piece is filed as well. Anyone filing by mail should include a return envelope with postage so the mailing charge is not added.

Lehigh County is in the Lehigh Valley, and Allentown is the county seat. The 2020 count was 374,557 people, of whom 125,845 lived in Allentown, and the 2025 estimate is 384,383. Housing runs from the oldest buildings in the county, such as Shelter House in Emmaus, built in 1734, to newer construction. Older homes can bring title questions like old easements or a lien that was never released, and the recording office's records can help answer them.

faqs.q: What is the Lehigh County recording fee for a deed?
faqs.a: A deed costs $81.25 under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. That covers four pages, four names and one PIN certification, with extra pages at $2.00 and extra names at $0.50.

faqs.q: Where is the Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in Room 122 of the courthouse at 455 W. Hamilton Street in Allentown. It is open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon, and the number is 610-782-3162.

faqs.q: Can I get a certified copy of a Lehigh County deed online?
faqs.a: No, they are made only at the office. Each certified copy adds $1.50 per document to the usual charge of $0.50 per page in person.

faqs.q: How far back do Lehigh County records go?
faqs.a: Records begin in 1812. LANDEX covers index, deed, mortgage, map and miscellaneous records from that year to today.

faqs.q: Are Lehigh County deeds recorded the same day?
faqs.a: Electronic filings through Simplifile, CSC or ePN are usually recorded the same day. Paper filings depend on the queue, and a rejected paper filing costs $10.00.
